title: Open stabilizer-preserving locus for a representable unramified map
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic stacks mean [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces mean [def-trf-algebraic-space], and stacks, representability and 2-fibre products mean [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable morphism properties are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Flatness, local finite presentation, etaleness and properness use [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. A stack morphism is separated if its relative diagonal is proper. The inertia stack $I_{\mathcal A}$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows given by conjugating isomorphisms. Its projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The set $|\mathcal A|$ consists of field-valued objects up to isomorphism after common field extension, with the atlas topology [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be representable by algebraic spaces and unramified, and suppose $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ is proper. Here unramifiedness uses [def-weil-unramified-morphism] on etale scheme charts. The locus of points $a\in|\mathcal A|$ at which $f$ induces an isomorphism of stabilizer group algebraic spaces is an open subset. It defines an open substack $\mathcal A^\circ\subseteq\mathcal A$, and the natural map $I_{\mathcal A^\circ}\to\mathcal A^\circ\times_{\mathcal B}I_{\mathcal B}$ is an isomorphism. In particular, for $f$ representable by algebraic spaces and etale, with finite target inertia, every point where stabilizers agree belongs to such an open substack. An open substack means a strictly full substack (closed under isomorphism) whose scheme base changes are open subschemes.

source.place: Tag 0DUA (lemma-stabilizer-preserving-unramified), including the inertia-isomorphism conclusion; etale implies unramified and finite implies proper for its stated special case.

proof.text: For any scheme $T$ and object $a:T\to\mathcal A$, let $G_T=\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal A}(a)$ and $H_T=\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal B}(f(a))$, as sheaves on $T$-schemes. These are algebraic spaces: $T\times_{\mathcal A}T$ and $T\times_{\mathcal B}T$ are algebraic spaces by [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], and their pullbacks along $\Delta_T:T\to T\times_kT$ give $G_T$ and $H_T$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A section of the first pullback is precisely an automorphism of $a$, and the second is the same construction for $f(a)$. This also identifies these spaces with the scheme pullbacks of the two inertia projections. All constructions commute with arbitrary scheme base change, since their sections are the same objects and arrows pulled back in the fibred groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 0DUA, first paragraph; Tag 0DU8 (remark-get-property-auts-from-diagonal), explicit automorphism spaces

proof.text: Put $X_T=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T$, using $f(a):T\to\mathcal B$. It is an algebraic space, unramified over the scheme $T$, by the hypothesis on $f$. Its section $x$ is $(a,\mathrm{id}_{f(a)})$. Over $H_T$ there is a second section $x_h=(a,h)$, where $h$ is the universal automorphism of $f(a)$. Equality of $x$ and $x_h$ in the sheaf $X_T$ means the existence of an arrow $v:a\to a$ with $h=f(v)$ (replace $h$ by its inverse if the opposite comparison convention is chosen). Such an arrow is unique because the base change $X_T$ is equivalent to a discrete groupoid. Thus $j_T:G_T\to H_T$ identifies with the pullback of $\Delta_{X_T/T}$ along $(x,x_h):H_T\to X_T\times_TX_T$. By [lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal] this diagonal is a representable open immersion. Its pullback is an open immersion too: on each scheme test it is a further scheme base change of an open immersion, to which [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] applies. Hence $j_T$ identifies $G_T$ with an open subspace of $H_T$.

source.place: Tag 0DU8 and Tag 0DUA, first paragraph; the open-immersion diagonal gives the representable case directly

proof.text: For a field-valued representative $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal A$, $j_K$ is the induced homomorphism of stabilizer group algebraic spaces, by step 1. It is an isomorphism exactly when the complement of its open image is empty, by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. This condition is unchanged by a field extension $L/K$: an open subspace with full point image equals its target, and a nonempty complement stays nonempty after field extension. For the latter assertion, apply the surjectivity of $|H_K\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L|\to|H_K|\times_{|\operatorname{Spec}K|}|\operatorname{Spec}L|$ in that node to any point of the complement; the pullback open image has the inverse-image point set. Isomorphic objects conjugate both automorphism groups and their comparison, so the condition is also invariant under isomorphism. It therefore defines a subset $W\subseteq|\mathcal A|$ independently of the representative.

source.place: Tag 0DTW (remark-identify-automorphism-groups), with the field-extension argument of lemma-iso-automorphism-groups; Tag 0DUA, second paragraph

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal A$, provided by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use $G=G_U$, $H=H_U$, and $q:H\to U$ from steps 1--2. The assumption that $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ is proper says precisely that this scheme base change $q$ is proper. In particular $|q|$ is closed: properness of algebraic spaces means separated, finite type and universally closed, as explicitly specified in [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. The subset $C=|H|\setminus|G|$ is closed. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], its intersection with the inverse image of $u\in U$ is empty exactly when the open immersion $G_u\to H_u$ is an isomorphism: the image formula for fibre products identifies the point image of the fibre, and an open subspace with full point image is the whole space. Thus $p^{-1}(W)=V=U\setminus q(C)$ is open, with no finiteness condition on $C$.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, closed-image argument in second paragraph; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZM (definition-proper)

proof.text: The atlas criterion in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] now shows that $W$ is open in $|\mathcal A|$. For $R=U\times_{\mathcal A}U$ the two maps to $U$ give isomorphic objects of $\mathcal A$; step 3 shows that the inverse images of $V$ have equal point subsets. They are open subspaces, so they are equal as subfunctors by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Consequently [lem-sfb-invariant-open-substack-descent], applied to this smooth atlas and its invariant open $V$, produces the strictly full algebraic open substack $\mathcal A^\circ$ with $U\times_{\mathcal A}\mathcal A^\circ=V$. Its point subset is $W$: atlas point-surjectivity and this pullback equality detect membership on $U$. This uses the invariant-open theorem for general algebraic stacks, rather than its Deligne--Mumford-only variant.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, construction of the open substack; stacks-properties.tex Tags 04XL, 0507 and 06FJ

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to\mathcal A^\circ$, repeat steps 1--2 with its object $a$. Strict fullness identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal A^\circ}(a)$ with $\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal A}(a)$, so the required inertia comparison pulls back to the open immersion $j_T:G_T\to H_T$. Every point of $H_T$ maps to a point $t$ of $T$. The object $a_t$ belongs to $W$, since $T$ maps to $\mathcal A^\circ$, hence $(j_T)_t$ is an isomorphism by step 3. The fibre-product point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] therefore shows that every point of $H_T$ lies in the open image of $j_T$. The full-point-image clause of that node makes $j_T$ an isomorphism. Thus, for every scheme $T$ and every object $a\in\mathcal A^\circ(T)$, every automorphism of $f(a)$ lifts uniquely to an automorphism of $a$, compatibly with pullback. These unique lifts give an inverse to the inertia comparison on objects $(a,h)$ and on conjugating arrows: if $f(v)h=h' f(v)$, uniqueness forces $v\alpha=\alpha' v$ for the lifted automorphisms. The constructions are inverse and natural. This proves the asserted isomorphism of inertia stacks without invoking fibrewise isomorphism for arbitrary morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0DUA, last sentence; explicit open-immersion proof of the Tag 0DU9 conclusion in the representable case

proof.text: Finally suppose $f$ is etale and $\mathcal B$ has finite inertia. Each scheme test of $f$ is unramified by the etale clause of [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence]. Each scheme base change of $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ is finite by hypothesis and hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Thus the hypotheses already treated hold, and every point where the stabilizers agree lies in the open substack constructed in step 5, with the inertia isomorphism proved in step 6.

That is the 0DU8 square for representable f, and the open-immersion property comes from lem-sfb-unramified-space-open-diagonal (05W1); this is correct. Step 6 shows the open immersion has full point image, so it is an isomorphism. Step 7 uses étale⇒unramified (06CR) and finite⇒proper (01WN).
